business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020) and its Implementing Regulations; Administrative Measures for Enterprise Information Disclosure; and SAMR rules implementing the National Beneficial Owner Information System, which is available exclusively to government authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: original notarized by a Taiwan district court notary; certified by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); verified by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); accepted by the Chinese market regulator. No Hague Apostille step is added because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention member.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Corporate Registry Record) of the Taiwan Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Taiwan notarization, SEF certification, ARATS verification, then SAMR acceptance. Parallel path; Hague Apostille is not applicable and is never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Taiwan Ultimate Parent approving the China WFOE formation, capital commitment, and UBO disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan parent, notarized by a Taiwan court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: notary certification in Taiwan, SEF certification, ARATS verification, then submission to SAMR and the Chinese bank. No Apostille chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of the Taiwan Ultimate Parent, including latest amendments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan MOEA certified copy; notarized by Taiwan court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: verification through SEF/ARATS; accepted by Chinese authorities, registry, and bank compliance units. Parallel to Apostille but mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the Taiwan parent's principal bank covering account conduct, creditworthiness, and beneficial owner confirmations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan bank licensed by the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Taiwan bank notarization/legalization via Taiwan court notary, SEF certification, ARATS verification, and submission to the Chinese bank. If the Chinese receiving bank accepts a certified true copy without SEF/ARATS, the AML officer still requires original or verified electronic authentication.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN/Non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, PRC MOFCOM Unreliable Entity List, PBOC money-laundering suspicious transaction lists, and any Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions/AML notices. Screen all UBOs, officers, directors, authorized signers, counterparties in LME warrant transfers and documentary LC chains, and beneficial owners of any intermediate holding entity. Enhanced due diligence requires source-of-wealth documents, negative news, PEP status (domestic/foreign/international organization PEPs per FATF), adverse media, and sanctions jurisdiction exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Online Declaration System (the nationwide enterprise name declaration system operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese name of the WFOE must use simplified Chinese characters; foreign-language names may be registered only as a supplementary name and must be consistent with the Chinese name. The statutory four-tier naming structure is: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry/operation characteristic + enterprise legal form, for example: [City/Province] [Zihao] Non-Ferrous Metals Trading (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. Foreign investors' transliterated names must follow official pinyin or an approved romanization and cannot misleadingly suggest a different ownership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the name application, the applicant must request a written statement of reasons from the local SAMR enterprise registration department. Within 15 days of receipt, the applicant may submit a formal written appeal to a higher-level market regulation bureau stating corrective amendments and legal basis. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may commence administrative reconsideration under the Administrative Reconsideration Law within 60 days, followed by an administrative lawsuit before the competent people's court within 15 days of the reconsideration decision. In parallel, counsel should prepare a revised name application to minimize loss of business continuity while preserving reservation priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PRC WFOE in wholesale base-metals trading (ISIC 4662), a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is operationally untenable. Tax authorities and banks will reject the registration for VAT invoice issuance and RMB/FX bank account opening because the actual place of business requirement under relevant PRC regulations cannot be satisfied. A registered shared office or co-working space may be accepted only if a legal lease is filed with the market regulator, the office has visible company signage, and the company maintains books, records, and personnel on site. A mere postal address without physical presence will trigger enhanced AML review and likely refusal of documentary LC facilities, LME warrant transfer instructions, and VAT general taxpayer designation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for a newly formed WFOE with a Taiwan parent and copper cathode trading scope, estimated at 75% risk if annual VAT invoice value exceeds RMB 5 million or if the entity applies for general VAT taxpayer status. Checklist: (1) lease in force and registered with the rental filing authority; (2) property ownership certificate or landlord authorization; (3) company name plate matching registered Chinese name; (4) occupied office furniture, computers, and staff; (5) books, vouchers, ledgers, and UBO records maintained at the address; (6) business license displayed; (7) utility invoices showing consumption at the address; (8) bank documents matching the registered address; (9) no shared multi-company mailbox/address that lacks partition or signage; (10) responsible person or authorized representative available during business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (公司法), as amended, Articles 1, 2, 4, 8, 18, 98, 100, 101, 102, 128, 129, 130, 156, 161, 161-1, 162, 172, 192, 202, 203, 208, 218-1, 228, 431; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 6, 7 and 8; Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment by Foreign Nationals; Commercial Registration Act and Fees Schedule issued by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan for pre-incorporation foreign investment approval; Commerce Development Administration, MOEA, Taiwan (Company Registration Section) for statutory incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form together with the approved Foreign Investment Approval Letter, Articles of Incorporation, capital verification report, director and shareholder consent certificates, and registered office proof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Company Act. There is no statutory minimum paid-in capital requirement and no blocked escrow account obligation. However, the foreign investor must obtain an Investment Commission approval letter before remitting capital into Taiwan, and the remitted funds must be held in a Taiwanese bank account and verified by a certified public accountant before the incorporation filing can be completed. The approved capital amount must be reasonably proportionate to the stated wholesale copper cathode trading scope and the WFOE's payment rails, including documentary letters of credit and LME warrant transfers.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [WFOE NAME] COPPER TRADING LIMITED

The Board of Directors of [WFOE NAME] Copper Trading Limited (the Company), having been lawfully designated by the sole shareholder, met at the registered office in Taipei, Taiwan on [date] at [time]. A quorum was present. The Chairman confirmed that the meeting was held with due notice and in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation.

WHEREAS the sole shareholder has unconditionally subscribed for the entire initial paid-in share capital of the Company, comprising [●] ordinary shares of par value NT$10 each, at an aggregate subscription price of NT$[●]; and

WHEREAS the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs has granted approval No. [●] on [●]; and

WHEREAS the Company requires a registered office, banking arrangements, statutory officers, and corporate governance machinery to receive legal process and to transact its wholesale physical arbitrage business in Grade A refined copper cathodes, ISIC 4662; and

WHEREAS the Company's commercial model involves LME warrant transfers, documentary letters of credit, and settlement in accordance with the applicable banking and AML/CFT rules;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AND ORDERED as follows:

1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The share subscription by the sole shareholder is ratified and confirmed. The Board authorizes the Chairman to execute and issue share certificates, to record the shareholder in the register of members, and to take all necessary steps to comply with Article 162 of the Taiwan Company Act.

2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is adopted and fixed at [●], [District], Taipei, Taiwan. The Chairman is authorized to execute the lease, to file the address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and to receive all legal process, notices, and government correspondence at such registered office.

3. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following appointments are approved and effective immediately: [●] as Director and Chairman; [●] as General Manager; [●] as Chief Accountant; and [●] as Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer. Each officer shall exercise all powers and duties prescribed by the Taiwan Company Act, the Articles of Incorporation, and the Company's internal financial and AML control policies applicable to commodity commodity trading.

4. Banking Authorization and Payment Rails. The Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts, including a New Taiwan Dollar operating account, a United States Dollar settlement account, a documentary letter-of-credit account, and any account needed to receive and transfer LME warrants or title documents, with [●] Bank, Taiwan, or another bank licensed by the Ministry of Finance. The Chairman and General Manager, acting jointly, and any two of the Chairman, General Manager, and Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer, are authorized to sign, execute, endorse, and process wire transfers, letters of credit, bankers' acceptances, guarantees, derivative margin postings, and copper cathode trade settlement documents in accordance with the Company's two-person control policy.

5. Regulatory Filing Authorization. The Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer is directed to complete the MOEA company registration, the Ministry of Finance tax registration, the Directorate General of Customs importer and exporter registration, and any subsequent filing required by the Central Bank or local authorities, respecting all statutory deadlines.

6. Ratification of Preliminary Expenditures. All notarial, legal, registration, filing, lease, banking, and advisory expenses lawfully incurred in connection with the formation of the Company are ratified, approved, and directed to be paid.

All resolutions were passed unanimously and declared immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; online filing through the Investment Commission foreign investment e-filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign parent shareholder must submit a formal foreign investment application before any capital remittance, declaring the precise scope of wholesale physical arbitrage in Grade A refined copper cathodes, source of funds, proposed capital amount, Taiwan counterparties, and AML/KYC information. Foreign corporate documents must be legalized or apostilled and accompanied by certified Chinese or English translations. The local agent must submit the application with a power of attorney, audited financial statements or bank references, a detailed business plan, and beneficial ownership disclosures. The Investment Commission will review the investment for compliance with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, national security restrictions, and industry eligibility. A written Foreign Investment Approval Letter must be issued before proceeding to bank account opening and capital remittance.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certificate of incorporation or equivalent good standing certificate of the foreign investing company
Passport or corporate authorization of the ultimate beneficial owner
Audited financial statements or bank reference letters for the past two years
Power of attorney in favor of the Taiwan local agent
Detailed business plan covering copper cathode procurement, LC payment flows, and LME warrant settlement
AML/KYC declaration and beneficial ownership structure chart
Certified translation of foreign corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a supplemental information request, the applicant has 60 days to cure deficiencies or the application will lapse. If the application is denied, the foreign investor may file an administrative appeal with the Minister of Economic Affairs or an administrative petition under the Administrative Appeal Act, Taiwan, within 30 days of receipt of the denial. Any material change in shareholder, capital, or business scope requires a prior amendment application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Remittance, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A foreign-exchange-designated bank authorized by the Central Bank of China, Taiwan, together with a certified public accountant licensed by the Financial Supervisory Commission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the local agent must open a temporary corporate bank account in the Company's name at a Taiwan banking institution. The foreign shareholder must remit the approved paid-in capital from its home country through normal banking channels and ensure the remittance is identified with the investment approval number. The bank will file the foreign exchange inward remittance with the Central Bank and issue a bank statement and balance certificate. A certified public accountant must inspect the remittance advices, bank statements, and share subscription records, and issue a capital verification report confirming that the paid-in capital is fully received and lawfully held. Funds cannot be withdrawn for ordinary business purposes until the Company is incorporated, except for permitted pre-incorporation expenses.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Bank account application form and KYC forms
Corporate power of attorney and resolution authorizing account opening
Capital remittance advices or SWIFT MT103 messages
Bank certificate of receipt and balance
CPA capital verification report
Passport or ID copies of authorized signatories
AML beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses or queries the remittance, the applicant should resubmit corrected source and purpose codes with the Investment Commission approval letter. If the received capital exceeds the approved amount by more than twenty percent, the Company must first apply to the Investment Commission for an approved capital increase before incorporation. If the capital verification statement disagrees with the approved investment amount, the foreign investor must file an amendment with the Commission before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commerce Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, Company Registration Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the capital verification report is issued, the local agent must file the incorporation application with MOEA together with the Articles of Incorporation, the Investment Commission approval, director and shareholder consents, registered office lease or title evidence, and proof of the capital verification report. MOEA will examine the company name, business scope, legality of share capital, statutory officers, and registered office. The company becomes a juridical person only upon MOEA approval and issuance of the Company Registration Certificate. The WFOE's articles should state the corporate name, whether in Chinese or a Romanized English name, its legal seat in Taiwan, capital, share class, directors, and governance rules. After approval, the company must immediately proceed to tax registration and customs registration.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation signed by the sole shareholder
CPA capital verification report
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Consent letters and identification documents of directors and shareholders
Registered office lease agreement or proof of ownership
Company name reservation certificate, if any
Registration fee payment receipt
Representative and local agent power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a query or suspends the registration, the applicant must correct or supplement the filing within 30 days. If the registration is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days after the written rejection is served. In practice, the fastest cure is to amend the Articles of Incorporation, correct the capital verification statement, or revise the registered office proof and re-file without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Customs, and Statutory Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; Directorate General of Customs, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; local labor and health authorities; and the company's chosen commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after incorporation, the Company must register with the National Taxation Bureau to obtain its Uniform Identification Number and uniform invoice supplier qualification. The Company must also apply for importer and exporter registration with the Directorate General of Customs if it will physically import or export copper cathodes or clear LME warrant cargoes. The Company must open its operational VAT invoice register, establish documentary letter of credit and trade settlement accounts, and complete all commercial bank AML/CFT onboarding requirements. If the Company later occupies its own warehouse for physical copper cathode inventory, the local Fire Department approval must be obtained before occupancy; if inventory is held in third-party public warehouses, the warehouse operator's permits must be contractually verified.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate issued by MOEA
Company seal and registered corporate bank account certificate
Tax registration application form
Director and shareholder identification documents
Uniform Invoice application, if applicable
Importer and exporter registration application with customs
Registered office lease and utility invoice
AML/CFT questionnaire and corporate register
Warehouse operator permit certificate only if company-operated storage is planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is late, the Company should file a late registration request with an explanation to the local National Taxation Bureau and pay any administrative penalty. If customs registration is queried, the Company must align the imported commodity description with the MOEA business scope and submit the tax Identification Number and company registration certificate through the Customs Single Window. If a company-operated warehouse is planned and the fire inspection is not passed, occupancy must be deferred until the Fire Department certifies the fire safety management plan and equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The WFOE is engaged solely in wholesale physical arbitrage of Grade A refined copper cathodes under ISIC 4662, which is not a manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or employer-operated warehousing activity. No industrial factory registration, manufacturing license, or fixed pollution source permit is required for the approved trading scope. If the Company later operates its own warehouse, the applicable authorities would be the local municipal Fire Department and the Commerce Development Administration / Economic Development Bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operating license or factory registration certificate is triggered by pure wholesale trading of non-ferrous copper cathodes. The only mandatory operational registrations are the MOEA company registration, Ministry of Finance tax and uniform invoice registration, and Directorate General of Customs importer and exporter registration. Copper cathodes are not a restricted chemical, defense-related, or strategic commodity under the applicable Taiwan regulatory framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Triggered. Pure wholesale trading of inert Grade A refined copper cathodes is not a listed Category I or Category II environmental facility under the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act. No full EIA report, environmental impact statement, or project environmental review is required for an office-based metal trading company. If the Company later establishes an industrial site involving copper melting, refining, electroplating, or acid treatment, a project environmental review or fixed pollution source permit may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Triggered for the approved activity. Copper cathodes are inert metals; no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation arises from trading, transfer of LME warrants, or storage in third-party bonded or public warehouses. If the Company later operates a warehouse, any domestic sewage must be discharged into a sanitary sewer and must meet the general Water Pollution Control Act pH 6 to 9 standard; copper cathode surfaces and packaging must be kept dry and clean; any contaminated sludges, acidic electrolyte residue, or hazardous packaging must be characterized under Taiwan Waste Disposal Act categories and handled by licensed waste transporters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to the registered office or office-based trading activity. If the WFOE later operates or controls its own warehouse, the operator must obtain a Fire Safety Management Plan approval and an inspection certificate from the local municipal Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, Taiwan, covering fire-extinguishing equipment, exit signage, and evacuation plans. A structural load and building code safety clearance may be required for the storage of palletized copper cathodes. Occupational safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is required for manual handling operations, forklifts, emergency response planning, and copper dust control. For third-party warehouse storage, the WFOE must contractually require the warehouse operator to maintain current fire and occupational safety certifications.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and the national unified Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Taxation) portal, which is the statutory online system for taxpayer registration, tax returns, VAT invoice administration, and export tax rebate processing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the STA assigns the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) upon completion of company registration with the Market Regulation Administration; the USCC is the taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration number. No separate manual TIN application is required for the WFOE. A foreign non-resident enterprise that has not established a Chinese entity but derives Chinese-source income or creates a permanent establishment must file for non-resident tax registration through the e-Taxation portal with the local STA office, providing the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, identity documents of responsible persons, and, where applicable, a China tax representative appointment letter. A foreign enterprise that only receives China-source passive income subject to withholding is not ordinarily required to obtain a full TIN; the Chinese withholding payer completes the withholding and reporting obligations. The WFOE should then confirm VAT taxpayer status (general or small-scale) and register for export tax rebate eligibility through the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not have check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. A WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a Chinese resident enterprise on its worldwide income; the only relevant statutory election is the VAT taxpayer status election between general VAT taxpayer and small-scale VAT taxpayer, subject to the RMB 5,000,000 turnover threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Any person engaged in taxable sales in mainland China must complete tax registration at the competent STA office; annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 mandate general VAT taxpayer registration, while turnover of RMB 5,000,000 or below normally qualifies for small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment with a 3% collection rate, unless voluntary general taxpayer status is elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA's electronic invoice issuance system and the national Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform, with real-time data transmission to the Golden Tax system (Golden Tax Project Phase IV) for invoice matching, anti-fraud analysis, and risk control. Large taxpayers may integrate system-to-system API invoicing; VAT special invoices are subject to statutory controls on sequence numbers, passwords, and stamping, and any unreported or false invoicing is subject to severe administrative and criminal penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT general taxpayer may apply the 0% export VAT rate to physical export sales of Grade A copper cathodes where the goods are lawfully declared to mainland China Customs and physically exported from mainland China customs territory, the export sale is made to an overseas buyer, delivery is substantiated by transport documentation, and the export proceeds are repatriated to China within the statutory period. Exports to the Taiwan customs territory are eligible on the same cross-border export basis. Qualifying offshore services consumed wholly outside China may also be zero-rated, but the primary commodity scope here is physical copper cathode arbitrage.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Goods Declaration Form (Export Customs Declaration/Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from mainland China
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the exporting WFOE
Export sales contract or purchase order

Bank entry or settlement proof evidencing receipt of foreign exchange or cross-border RMB from the Taiwan or other overseas buyer, including the Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank remittance advice
Inspection certificate, certificate of origin, or other export control document required for the commodity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the tax authority determines that the export was fictitious, the goods did not physically leave the customs territory, the export declaration was false, or foreign exchange was not repatriated within the prescribed deadline, the claimed zero rate or export VAT refund will be clawed back in full with late payment surcharge. The exporter becomes liable for VAT at the standard 13% rate and may be fined under the Law on Tax Collection and Administration and the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China. Fraudulent export-refund schemes constitute tax evasion crimes under the Criminal Law and expose the entity and responsible officers to criminal penalties, loss of export rebate status, and public tax blacklisting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) with delegated State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is not freely convertible on capital account. Current-account trade transactions are convertible under a bank-led true-trade verification framework, but capital-account items such as paid-in capital, shareholder loans and equity repatriation are subject to SAFE registration, use restrictions and negative-list screening. Taiwan-sourced investment in a Chinese wholesale WFOE enters through a designated FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and must be settled strictly in accordance with the approved capital purpose; funds may not be redirected to prohibited activities such as unauthorized mainland equity investment or unapproved entrusted lending. Dividend remittance to the Taiwan parent is permitted only after audited financial statements are prepared, the corporate income tax filing is completed and tax clearance is evidenced, and the bank has received a board resolution plus the underlying capital registration documents. Export proceeds from copper cathode re-exports are not subject to a mandatory conversion ratio, but they must be repatriated to China through an authorized bank and must pass the trade authenticity review involving invoice, customs declaration, bill of lading and payment matching. The practical hurdles are documentary: banks require precise purpose-coding, timely SAFE updating, and clean matching between physical trade and financial flows for RMB to be settled without delay.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to China through an authorized bank; for general trade in goods the collection is expected to be completed within 90 days from customs export declaration unless longer trade terms up to 180 days have been properly recorded in the bank's trade credit system. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain foreign currency in a settlement account or convert to RMB at market rates, subject to same-bank verification of the underlying export contracts, customs declarations, inspection certificates and payment flows. Any prolonged overdue export collection or unexplained partial collection will trigger enhanced AML review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account; RMB Basic Deposit and Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and CNY Operational Settlement Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account; Export Proceeds Current Account; Documentary LC Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and RMB Basic Account with Trade Finance Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under PBOC and SAFE regulations, only designated authorized banks can open and operate FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Accounts, accept or settle export proceeds, perform FX conversion, and clear documentary credits. Fintech EMIs and third-party payment institutions are not licensed as SAFE-designated banks for capital-account remittances and cannot issue or confirm commercial L/Cs, manage LME warrant clearing, or act as the WFOE's primary treasury clearing rail. They may be used only for ancillary domestic collection convenience; they must remain subordinate to the bank documentation flow and cannot replace the statutory KYC/AML filing. A compliant treasury structure should therefore be built on Tier-1 domestic commercial banks, with no reliance on offshore EMI gateways for inbound FDI or physical copper settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required for the legal representative and at least one authorized corporate signatory for the initial China on-boarding at the bank branch. The bank will also perform a site-visit and integrity verification of the registered office and substantive copper cathode operations. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for an FDI capital account; if Taiwan-based shareholders cannot appear in mainland China, a notarized and duly authenticated power of attorney may be accepted, but the authorized individual must still pass an in-person AML interview and the ultimate beneficial owner declaration must be documented. Enhanced due diligence for medium-risk, cross-border commodity trading may also require annual reviews and refreshed KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait beneficial ownership opacity: Taiwan-sourced shareholders using family trusts or shell transit companies leave the ultimate human owners unidentifiable.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Taiwan company registry extracts, certified shareholder register, UBO declaration form, national identity and passport copies for every natural-person owner, full corporate chain chart, audited financial statements and bank reference letters of each investing entity, source-of-wealth evidence, and notarized and authenticated documents to satisfy Chinese bank acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering signals in Grade A copper cathode operations: unstable invoice premiums, frequent beneficiary substitution, or LME warrant transfers without matching physical cargo documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master purchase agreements, refiner production certificates and LME warrant trail, independent inspection certificates from SGS or Bureau Veritas, complete ocean or airway bills and delivery orders, customs declarations, original commercial invoices and packing lists, contract pricing formula including premium and discount fix records, and bank statements evidencing identical cash-flow paths.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or export-control flags: consignees or routing ports with inconsistent trade history or transmission through jurisdictions causing heightened geopolitical risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results of all counterparties and UBOs against PBOC, SAFE, UN, OFAC and EU sanctions lists; written end-user and end-use declarations from each buyer; destination and re-export compliance certificate; loading and discharging port evidence; logistics contracts; compliance attestation that copper cathodes will be used for legitimate industrial wholesale and not diverted to embargoed programs; bank risk committee approval memo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI remittance mismatch: Taiwan shareholder remits equity capital without the SAFE FDI registration code, overstates the registered capital, or the remittance narrative is inconsistent with direct investment purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: WFOE business license, Foreign Investment Information Report, SAFE FDI basic registration form and registration reference, Articles of Association and capital schedule, board resolution for the capital injection, notarized power of attorney for banking signatories, the Taiwan remitter's instruction carrying the SAFE registration reference and equity injection purpose, and a post-receipt capital verification report issued by a Chinese certified public accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity funding from Taiwan must use SWIFT MT103 from a Taiwan bank to the WFOE's designated FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a SAFE-listed Chinese commercial bank. The remittance instructions must carry the SAFE FDI registration reference and the correct balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment capital contribution; the bank will validate the code against the FDI registration form and the Articles of Association. After receipt, the bank performs capital account reporting, and the WFOE must obtain a CPA capital verification report within the statutory filing period. The funds may then be converted to RMB and transferred to the RMB basic account only after bank confirmation that the use is within business scope and not on the Foreign Investment Negative List. No third-party payment rail or unlicensed EMI may be used for this capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 is used for direct open-account and spot settlements to international copper suppliers, with invoices, warehouse warrants and transport documents pre-validated by the bank. Commercial Letters of Credit are advised via SWIFT MT700 and amendments via MT707; the issuing domestic bank pays complying presentations by MT103 or MT202 after checking bills of lading, LME warrant transfer instruction, quality and quantity certificates. Documentary Collections in the form of D/P or D/A may be used for approved counterparties, with the bank acting as collecting and advising agent, but they are weaker risk mitigation than LCs for high-value non-ferrous commodity flows. All outbound disbursements must be coded under the bank's trade-in-goods reporting framework and kept fully traceable to the physical copper transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts for genuine underlying trade or capital exposure, supported by contracts, invoices, customs declarations and flow forecasts, booked through an SAFE-qualified Chinese bank.
CNY/FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency shareholder loans or long-term trade financing, subject to SAFE registration and real business-need verification.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not generally permissible for an onshore resident WFOE as a standalone hedge; offshore NDFs may be considered only at the Taiwan parent level with licensed offshore banks and should never be used as speculative onshore products unless an explicit SAFE exception exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 30) with CPA-attested financial statements where statutory or tax thresholds apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (applicable regional administration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayer: file on or before 31 May of the following year; where a CPA-attested report and approved extension apply, filing may be extended to 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues a surcharge of 3% for each 30-day period up to a maximum of 30% of the assessed tax, plus statutory interest from the original due date; understatement or evasion may attract a penalty of 1.5 times the shortfall under Income Tax Act Articles 108 and 110. Persistent non-payment enables the National Taxation Bureau to levy assets and may lead MOEA to revoke company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting resolution approving financial statements, accounts, and profit distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting; minutes filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) company registration office and, where foreign-investment approval items have changed, with the MOEA Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year, i.e. by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual shareholders meeting within the statutory window permits the competent authority to order convening; directors who ignore such an order may be fined NT$10,000 to NT$50,000. Repeated non-compliance is an administrative trigger for dissolution or strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax pre-payment (semi-annual advance tax remittance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 July and 31 July of the current taxable year for a calendar-year company; the statutory amount is generally 50% of the prior-year taxable income unless an estimated return is filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or non-payment by 31 July triggers a late-payment surcharge of 1% for every two days up to 15% of the unpaid amount, plus statutory interest; continued delinquency allows tax seizure and enforcement, and can result in business tax registration revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding, Salary, Remittance and Income Self-Withholding Statements (year-end reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the following year for salaries, rents, professional fees, royalties, and foreign-remittance withholdings paid during the prior calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-reporting may expose the company to fines of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000 under Income Tax Act Article 114, or 3% of the unreported amount if greater; unpaid withheld taxes also accrue the 1% per-two-day late surcharge up to 15% and may lead to enforced collection and withholding-agent disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Operations and Investment Status Report (foreign investment annual survey / reporting obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year, or by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE; any foreign-investment shareholding or capital alteration must additionally be reported to MOEAIC within 30 days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to answer the MOEAIC statutory survey or to report approved foreign-investment changes may result in remedial notices, administrative fines, restriction of foreign-exchange remittance or capital repatriation privileges, and ultimately revocation of the foreign investment approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (VAT) Return - recurring bi-monthly statutory filings covering zero-rated physical copper cathode export trades and domestic sales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (VAT administration), Ministry of Finance; local revenue service for business tax registration matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing and payment by the 15th day of the month following each two-month period: Jan-Feb by 15 Mar; Mar-Apr by 15 May; May-Jun by 15 Jul; Jul-Aug by 15 Sep; Sep-Oct by 15 Nov; Nov-Dec by 15 Jan of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax due attracts a fine of NT$3,000; late filing with tax due attracts an additional 15% penalty tax and a monthly late-payment surcharge of 1% per two days up to 15%, plus statutory interest. Serious or repeated evasion may trigger business tax registration revocation and criminal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit under Taiwan Companies Act Article 20 applies to: (i) all public companies; (ii) non-public companies with paid-in capital of NT$30,000,000 or more; (iii) banking, insurance, securities, futures, bills finance and financial holding companies regardless of capital; (iv) any company ordered by MOEA or the Financial Supervisory Commission due to its business scope, public interest, or foreign-investment characteristics; and (v) tax-registered profit-seeking enterprises whose annual revenue exceeds NT$50,000,000, which must have income tax returns attested by a licensed CPA and may require transfer-pricing documentation. There is no standalone universal balance-sheet or headcount audit trigger for an ordinary non-public WFOE; however, the competent authorities may impose a certified audit where balance-sheet size, headcount, or AML/CFT profile warrants it, and a copper cathode wholesale WFOE with LME warrant transfers and documentary credit activity will normally be treated as requiring enhanced professional assurance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Commercial Accounting Act and its enforcement rules; Taiwan Financial

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax) plus a 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed net earnings
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying R&D expenditures may be claimed as an investment tax credit under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; technology license income from Taiwanese patents may qualify for a half-rate exemption under the IP Box-like regime; no universal free-zone corporate tax holiday applies, but bonded/free-trade-zone logistics and offshore warrant transfers may affect taxable sourcing; foreign tax credits and treaty credits are available only where substantiated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (CIT return) filed electronically through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Tax E-Filing Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw); XML schema and publication version are updated annually and approved for the applicable fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return, together with a provisional/estimated income tax return and payment due in September for calendar-year taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within five months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal-year-end, the return is due no later than May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: registered Chinese name of the Taiwan WFOE, tax identification number, legal form, registered address, industry code, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter CN_WFOE_LTD as a Taiwan-resident profit-seeking enterprise; disclose the non-resident Chinese parent in the shareholder schedule and complete the non-resident identification fields; attach the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, and proof of capital registration; confirm that the Taiwan entity is a local operating company and not a branch of the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis, financial accounting standards, inventory valuation method, and fiscal year selection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accrual basis and Taiwan IFRS; recognize copper cathode sales and LME warrant transfers on trade date, not settlement date; record mark-to-market changes for commodity derivatives; maintain daily Taiwan-dollar foreign exchange rates and LME settlement price documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues and sales: all proceeds from wholesale physical arbitrage of Grade A refined copper cathodes, including LME warrant deliveries, physical settlement premiums, and sale spread.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue on a gross basis, do not net LME warrant acquisition cost against sales; include all Taiwan-source and foreign-source trading revenue derived through the Taiwan entity; reconcile invoice value, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, LC payments, and LME trade confirmations; related-party sales must be recorded at the arm's-length price.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: commodity cost, warrant acquisition cost, freight, insurance, storage, broker fees, and other direct acquisition costs for copper cathodes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply specific identification or perpetual inventory method for each LME warrant lot; support each cost element with warehouse receipts, smelter export documents, shipping documents, and broker contracts; disallow inflated intercompany purchase prices that lack benchmark support; inventory write-downs must comply with Taiwan tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: selling, general, administrative, logistics, bank and LC charges, professional fees, insurance, and employee compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly related to earning taxable income are deductible; management fees or service fees paid to the Chinese parent or to any offshore related party must satisfy the real-service test and arm's-length requirement; cross-border service and royalty payments are subject to 20% withholding if taxable to the non-resident payee; disguised profit transfers are non-deductible and subject to recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating profit or loss: gross revenue less cost of goods sold and operating expenses before non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compare the reported net margin and gross margin of copper cathode trading with the Taiwan transfer-pricing benchmark; if the result falls outside the interquartile range under TNMM or an equivalent method, adjust to the arm's-length median; insufficient documented economic substance will trigger audit and profit reallocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and deductions: interest income, foreign-exchange gains/losses, commodity derivative gains/losses, dividend income, and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign-exchange gains and losses using Taiwan central bank spot rates; report LME warrants and derivatives separately from physical commodity revenue; foreign-source income and foreign taxes paid should be identified in the reconciliation schedule; non-resident parent dividend income is not to be consolidated except as required by law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before net operating loss deduction: net business income plus non-operating income less non-operating deductions, adjusted for statutory disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back fines, penalties, entertainment expenses exceeding statutory caps, related-party fees lacking substance, and intercompany interest that fails the thin-capitalization and arm's-length tests; include any prospective transfer-pricing adjustment identified by the taxpayer in the statutory adjustment line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforward deduction from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only assessed, reported, and audited prior-year losses may be carried forward for up to 10 years; the ownership-continuity and business-continuity tests must be satisfied; prepare a detailed schedule showing loss vintage, original assessed amount, amounts previously deducted, and current-year deduction; losses from foreign permanent establishments cannot reduce Taiwan taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after deduction of carryforward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the amount subject to the 20% Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax; reconcile from book net income using all permanent and temporary differences; ensure that no dividend distribution to the non-resident parent is deducted; the retained-earnings surtax is computed separately and not deducted here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computation: regular 20% tax, alternative minimum tax (AMT) base, and tax payable before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 20% corporate rate to taxable income; compute the AMT by adding tax-exempt investment income, certain insurance or securities gains, and other preference items; the greater of normal tax and AMT is payable; do not apply any treaty rate at this stage because withholding tax relief for outbound distributions is separate from the entity's own income tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments: investment tax credits, R&D credits, foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and provisional tax payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the statutory credit schedules for qualifying R&D and other investment incentives; report any Taiwan withholding tax suffered on third-party interest, royalties, or other income; offset the September provisional payment against the annual tax due; non-resident shareholder tax credits cannot be claimed by the Taiwan entity; excess credits are refundable only under applicable law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after credits and retained-earnings surtax; final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the final balance is paid by the statutory due date of May 31; the 5% retained-earnings surtax applies to undistributed post-tax earnings not distributed by the associated election date; if a dividend will be paid to the Chinese parent, the withholding tax must be computed and remitted according to the statutory 20% non-resident rate or applicable treaty rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return triggers a delinquency surcharge of 3% of the unpaid tax for every full two months of delay, subject to a maximum of 15%, plus daily late-payment interest; under-reporting or overstating deductions in a filed return is subject to an additional tax under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act of twice the underpaid amount, while fraudulent non-filing and tax evasion attract criminal penalties under Articles 41 and 47 of the Tax Collection Act, including imprisonment for up to five years and monetary fines; a responsible director may also face a travel restriction and asset preservation under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act where delinquent taxes exceed the statutory threshold and dissipation of assets is suspected.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends paid to a non-resident profit-seeking enterprise shareholder; 21% if the shareholder is a non-resident individual; under the Taiwan-China Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement, the source-state rate may be reduced to 5% for a beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the Taiwan payor's capital and to 10% in all other eligible ownership situations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on an outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payment to a Chinese-resident parent, the following procedural chain is mandatory: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the State Taxation Administration of China identifying the beneficial owner as a Chinese tax resident; (2) prepare and maintain a beneficial ownership declaration, corporate register, shareholding diagram, and board resolution proving that the Chinese recipient is not a pass-through conduit or commissionaire; (3) submit to the Taiwan payor the prescribed Treaty Benefit Application Form and supporting TRC before the payment date, generally through the National Taxation Bureau responsible for the Taiwan WFOE; (4) establish the substantive ownership threshold, holding period, and absence of a permanent establishment in Taiwan to which the income is effectively connected; (5) the Taiwan withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate at source; and (6) retain the full relief file for at least seven years to withstand a beneficial-ownership audit; failure to file before the due tax return is made will require a refund application and may trigger a 20% withholding deficiency plus interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Taiwan withholding rate for royalties paid to a non-resident is 20%, and the statutory withholding rate for interest paid to a non-resident is also 20%; under the Taiwan-China Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement, eligible royalties may be reduced
